title: Thoracic FSU absolute IDP under pure moments 0-7.5 Nm (all levels pooled)

quantity.name: IDP
quantity.definition: absolute nucleus pressure at 0/2.5/5/7.5 Nm, 3rd cycle; box plot median, q1, q3, whisker min/max (outliers excluded, listed in notes)

source.authors: Wilke HJ, Herkommer A, Werner K, Liebsch C
source.sample: human cadaver thoracic FSUs, fresh-frozen, rib stumps 20-30 mm, costovertebral joints kept; 30 FSUs from 19 donors (every level T1-T2 to T11-T12, >=1 per level)

protocol.summary: Thoracic FSUs (T1-T2 ... T11-T12) embedded half in PMMA, ribs shortened to 20-30 mm stumps with costovertebral joints intact; spine tester, pure moments up to 7.5 Nm in FE, LB, AR, 1 deg/s (FE, LB) and 0.5 deg/s (AR), 3.5 cycles, 3rd full cycle evaluated; no preload. IDP: 1.2 mm flexible sensor tube (MIPM FMSPEZ50, piezo-resistive tip) inserted from anterior centre into the centre of the nucleus, port pointing cranially, X-ray verified; absolute pressure read at 0, 2.5, 5.0, 7.5 Nm per direction (0 Nm = intrinsic pressure in that motion plane).
how_to_simulate: Model a thoracic FSU with rib stumps (costovertebral joints) and no anterior rib cage; fix the caudal vertebra, cranial vertebra free.
Apply pure moments 0-7.5 Nm in flexion, extension, left/right LB, left/right AR with no preload.
Read absolute nucleus pressure at 0, 2.5, 5.0 and 7.5 Nm; compare against the pooled all-level box plots (or level-specific when available).
protocol.notes: Pooled over all thoracic levels (Fig 3). Level/region effects: flexion IDP higher in T1-T5 than T8-T12 (Fig 4, r=-0.629 at 7.5 Nm), extension IDP higher in lower than upper thoracic at 7.5 Nm (r=0.500). Regional Figs 4-7 and the Supplementary Excel not extracted. Median intrinsic IDP (text): LB 0.058, AR 0.037, F/E 0.022 MPa; intrinsic range -0.052 to 0.175 MPa (median 0.037).
